ford/explorer.note: The Explorer is the clearest example on this site of a nameplate whose reputation depends entirely on the year. The fifth generation (2011–2019) opens well, then the 2013 and 2016 model years carry more than 2,000 complaints each, concentrated in the powertrain (the 2.0 and 2.3-litre EcoBoost engines and the six-speed automatic), power-steering assist loss, and the exhaust-odour issue that prompted a federal investigation into Police Interceptor and civilian Explorers. Ford issued technical service bulletins rather than a single recall for the exhaust problem, which is why it shows up as complaints rather than campaigns. The sixth generation launched in 2020 with a rough first year — transmission and electrical complaints climbed again — and settled from 2021. If you are buying used, the 2018–2019 and 2022–2023 model years are where the record is clean; treat 2013, 2016 and 2020 as years to walk past unless the price reflects the risk.

ford/escape.note: The third-generation Escape (2013–2019) launched with the 1.6-litre EcoBoost engine, and that engine is the reason the 2013 and 2014 model years carry the highest complaint counts of any compact crossover in the dataset: coolant leaks into the cylinders, overheating and engine fires, addressed by a string of recalls that continued for years. The 2.0-litre EcoBoost in the same body is a better engine, but the transmission and electrical complaints of the early years apply to both. Complaints fall sharply from 2015 and the 2016–2017 cars are the sweet spot of that generation. The 2018 year is an outlier again, and the fourth generation's first year, 2020, repeats the pattern seen across Ford's launches: a new platform, a new three-cylinder engine and an eight-speed automatic, and a jump in complaints that subsides by 2021. Hybrid versions from 2020 onward have a separate, quieter record.

ford/focus.note: The 2012–2016 Focus is the best-known transmission failure of its decade. Ford's PowerShift dual-clutch automatic (the DPS6) shuddered, slipped and lost drive, and the 2012 model year alone has close to 3,800 complaints on file — more than most nameplates accumulate across their entire run. Ford extended the clutch and control-module warranties, settled a class action, and the problem never fully went away on cars that keep the original design. The 2011 car, the last of the previous generation with a conventional automatic, scores 94 on this site; the 2015–2017 cars are better than 2012–2014 but still carry the same transmission. If you are considering a used Focus with PowerShift, ask for the clutch-replacement history and budget for it; a manual-gearbox car avoids the issue entirely, and the ST and RS are manual-only. The electric Focus has its own, much smaller record.

jeep/grand-cherokee.note: The WK2 Grand Cherokee (2011–2021) is a long-lived platform whose complaint record tells you which components Jeep fixed and when. The 2011–2012 years carry electrical complaints — the Totally Integrated Power Module, which controls fuel pump and lighting, was the subject of an investigation and a recall — along with the early Pentastar V6 cylinder-head issue. The 2014 year, the first with the ZF eight-speed automatic and the monostable electronic shifter, has the highest count of the generation; the shifter design was linked to rollaway incidents and recalled in 2016. From 2016 the record improves markedly and the 2017 and 2019–2020 years are among the best large SUVs on the site. The WL generation from 2022 has a moderate record so far, with infotainment and electrical complaints leading.

hyundai/sonata.note: The sixth-generation Sonata (2011–2014) is the car that brought Hyundai's Theta II engine problem into the open. Connecting-rod bearing failure in the 2.0 and 2.4-litre engines leads to knocking, stalling and, in the worst cases, fire; Hyundai recalled 2011–2014 Sonatas in 2015 and 2017, extended the engine warranty, installed a knock-sensor detection system, and in 2020 paid a civil penalty to the federal regulator over the timing of the recalls. The 2011 model year has more than 3,300 complaints on record and scores 24. The 2015–2017 seventh generation shares the engine and shares the pattern at a lower level. Everything changes with the 2018 and especially the 2019 model years, once the engines had been reworked and the fleet had been through the recall campaigns: the 2019–2025 Sonata is among the best-scoring family saloons on the site. Buy 2018 onward; if you buy earlier, verify the engine recall and the knock-sensor update have been completed.

ram/1500.note: The Ram 1500's record splits by generation. The fourth-generation truck (2009–2018, continued as the 1500 Classic to 2024) carries steady complaints about the air suspension, the electronic shifter, and — from 2013 when the eight-speed arrived — the transmission and the EcoDiesel V6, whose emissions recall and engine failures dominate the 2014–2016 counts. The fifth generation launched in 2019, and that first year has the highest count of the modern truck: the Uconnect infotainment screen delaminating, the eTorque mild-hybrid system, and electrical faults. From 2020 the record settles, and the truck scores in the 60s and 70s. A pre-purchase check on any Ram with air suspension is worth its cost; the coil-sprung trucks are simpler and cheaper to own.

honda/cr-v.note: For six years the fourth-generation CR-V (2012–2016) was one of the most dependable cars in the dataset, scoring in the 80s. Then the fifth generation arrived in 2017 with a 1.5-litre turbocharged engine, and the record turned: petrol diluting the engine oil in cold climates, rising oil levels, misfires and stalling, and a heater that would not warm the cabin in winter. Honda extended the warranty and issued software and hardware updates in 2018–2019 rather than a recall, so the problem lives in the complaint counts — 1,756 for 2017 and 2,119 for 2018. The 2020–2022 years show it fading. The sixth generation from 2023 opened with a new cluster of complaints, mostly electrical and infotainment, and its early years are scoring below the 2020–2022 cars. The CR-V Hybrid, available from 2020, has a cleaner record than the turbo petrol in every year.

jeep/cherokee.note: The KL Cherokee (2014–2023) launched with the first mass-market nine-speed automatic transmission, and that gearbox is the story of its early years: harsh shifts, hesitation, loss of drive, and repeated software reflashes that did not fully cure it. The 2014 model year has more than 2,600 complaints on record. Jeep improved the transmission calibration and hardware through 2016, and the counts fall accordingly, but the 2019 year — when the 2.0-litre turbo engine arrived alongside a facelift — spikes again. The 2020–2023 years are quiet and score well; they are the ones to buy. The Cherokee was discontinued after 2023.

ford/fusion.note: The Fusion's record has two separate problems in it. The 2010–2012 first generation carries complaints about the power steering (an electric-assist failure that was recalled) and the throttle body. The 2013–2020 second generation launched with the same 1.6-litre EcoBoost engine as the Escape and inherited its coolant and overheating problems, along with the 1.5-litre engine that replaced it and transmission complaints across the range. The 2016 model year carries a large share of the steering and transmission-shifter complaints of the facelifted car. The Fusion Hybrid's record is markedly cleaner from 2013 on — see its own page. The Fusion was discontinued in 2020.

kia/sorento.note: The Sorento shares Hyundai's Theta II 2.4-litre and 2.0-litre turbo engines, and the 2011 and 2016 model years are where its engine-failure complaints concentrate — the same bearing wear, knocking and stalling that hit the Sonata and Optima, covered by the same recall campaigns and warranty extensions. Between those years the record is moderate, and from 2018 the Sorento becomes one of the better three-row crossovers on the site, with the 2020 model year scoring 91. The fourth generation from 2021 introduced a new 2.5-litre turbo and a dual-clutch transmission; its complaint counts are low so far, with the dual-clutch attracting most of them.

honda/accord.note: The Accord has one of the longest clean stretches in the dataset, interrupted twice. The 2013 model year, the first of the ninth generation, carries complaints about the continuously variable transmission, the direct-injection four-cylinder's starter, and Bluetooth and infotainment faults. The 2018 model year, the first of the tenth generation, repeats the pattern with a 1.5-litre turbo that suffers the same oil-dilution problem as the CR-V, plus complaints about the heater and the infotainment screen. In both cases the second and third years of the generation are markedly better. The 2021–2024 cars score in the 70s and 80s. The Accord Hybrid, from 2014, has a separate and generally strong record.

chevrolet/malibu.note: The Malibu's record is defined by the 2013–2015 eighth generation's electrical and stop-start problems and by the 2016 ninth-generation launch, which brought a 1.5-litre turbo engine, a new eight-speed automatic and a spike to 1,669 complaints — hesitation, loss of power and transmission shudder. The 2017 and 2018 years are only marginally better. From 2019 the counts fall to a few hundred and the car scores in the 80s; a 2019–2023 Malibu is one of the better-value used saloons on the site. Chevrolet ended Malibu production in 2024.

jeep/wrangler.note: The JK Wrangler (2007–2018) has a moderate, consistent record — the 2011–2017 years score between 60 and 79 — with the usual Jeep electrical complaints and, on the earlier Pentastar engines, cylinder-head problems. The JL Wrangler launched for 2018 and its first year has the highest complaint count of any Wrangler on file: the 'death wobble' steering oscillation, welds on the frame, and the 2.0-litre turbo engine. Jeep replaced steering dampers under a customer-satisfaction programme in 2019 and revised the steering box. Counts halve for 2019 and again for 2020, but both still score below the JK's better years. Four-door Wranglers are catalogued separately as Wrangler Unlimited through 2020.

nissan/altima.note: The 2013–2015 Altima is the centre of Nissan's continuously variable transmission problem. The fifth-generation car launched with a Jatco CVT that overheated, shuddered, went into limp mode and, at worst, failed outright; the 2013 model year carries more than 2,300 complaints and scores 23. Nissan extended the transmission warranty on the 2013–2014 cars to seven years and settled a class action. From 2016 the transmission was revised and the record improves year on year; the 2019 onward sixth generation is a different car in the data, scoring in the 80s and 90s from 2021. A used 2013–2015 Altima should be priced for a transmission replacement unless one has already been done.

hyundai/elantra.note: The fifth-generation Elantra (2011–2016) carries complaints about the engine's piston-slap ticking, premature brake wear, and — with the highest counts — steering that pulls and wanders, which Hyundai addressed with a software update to the electric power steering. The 2011–2013 years are the worst of it; 2014–2016 score above 78. The sixth generation launched in 2017 with a jump in complaints, mostly engine and transmission, then settles: 2018 onward scores between 74 and 88. The Elantra does not use the Theta II engine at the centre of the Sonata recalls, so its engine complaints are of a different and less severe kind.

honda/pilot.note: The second-generation Pilot (2009–2015) is one of the quieter three-row SUVs in the dataset. The third generation arrived for 2016 with a nine-speed automatic on the upper trims, cylinder deactivation on the V6, and a new infotainment system — and 1,688 complaints: harsh and delayed shifts, warning-light cascades, and the engine idling roughly under cylinder deactivation. Honda reflashed the transmission and later replaced the nine-speed with its own ten-speed. The 2019 facelift year spikes again. The 2022–2024 fourth-generation cars score in the 70s. If you want a used Pilot, 2014–2015 or 2022 onward are the safe years.

subaru/outback.note: The Outback's record is quiet through the fourth and fifth generations apart from the FB25 engine's oil-consumption complaints on 2013–2014 cars, which Subaru settled with a class action. The sixth generation launched for 2020 on a new platform with a new infotainment system and a turbocharged 2.4-litre option, and the 2019–2020 years carry the highest counts in the Outback's history: the Starlink touchscreen freezing and rebooting, the battery draining, the windscreen cracking. From 2021 the counts fall and the 2023–2024 cars score in the 90s. The battery and windscreen complaints have been the subject of class-action litigation.

nissan/rogue.note: The Rogue is an unusual case: its complaint counts through the CVT era (2013–2018) are moderate rather than severe, because the Rogue's transmission calibration and cooling were revised earlier than the Altima's. The 2013–2018 years score between 65 and 83. The third generation launched for 2021 and the 2023 model year, when the 1.5-litre variable-compression three-cylinder engine became standard, has the highest count of any Rogue: engine noise, loss of power and stalling. That engine has been the subject of a federal investigation. The 2021–2022 cars with the 2.5-litre four-cylinder are the better buy.

kia/optima.note: The Optima shares the Sonata's Theta II engines and the same recall history, and its 2013 and 2015 model years carry the highest counts — engine knocking, stalling and fire risk, addressed by the 2017 recall and the extended engine warranty. From 2017 the Optima improves sharply, and the 2018–2020 cars score around 90. The nameplate was replaced by the K5 for 2021. As with the Sonata, an early Optima is a reasonable buy only if the engine recall, the knock-sensor update and, ideally, an engine replacement are documented.

chevrolet/equinox.note: The second-generation Equinox (2010–2017) with the 2.4-litre four-cylinder is known for consuming oil, which leads to timing-chain wear and, if neglected, engine failure; General Motors extended the warranty on the piston rings. The complaint counts are steady rather than spiking, and the 2016–2017 years score 86 and 91. The third generation from 2018 with the 1.5-litre turbo has a moderate record. The 2025 redesign opened with a jump in complaints and the lowest score in the Equinox's run, mostly electrical and infotainment. The sweet spot is 2016–2023.

hyundai/tucson.note: The third-generation Tucson launched for 2016 with a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission on the 1.6-litre turbo, and that transmission is the reason 2016 carries 1,616 complaints: hesitation from a standstill, jerking and loss of drive. Hyundai reflashed and, in some cases, replaced the transmission, and the 2018–2021 years score between 74 and 90. The fourth generation from 2022 opened with a new round of electrical and infotainment complaints, and the 2025 year is following the same pattern. The 2018–2021 cars, particularly with the naturally aspirated 2.0 and 2.4-litre engines and conventional automatic, are the ones to buy.

kia/soul.note: The second-generation Soul (2014–2019) carries the Gamma and Nu engines that were subject to Kia's engine-failure investigation and the 2019 recall for catalytic-converter damage leading to piston failure; the 2014–2016 years have the highest counts, with engine noise, stalling and fire cited. The 2017–2019 years are better, and the third generation from 2020 is quiet apart from a bump in 2020. A 2014–2016 Soul should have the engine recall and the knock-sensor update completed.

subaru/forester.note: The Forester's record mirrors the Outback's: oil-consumption complaints on the FB25 engine in 2014–2015, a long moderate stretch, and then a spike for the 2019 model year with the fifth generation's launch — the Starlink infotainment, battery drain, and the EyeSight driver-assistance system braking unnecessarily. The 2021–2024 years score between 83 and 91. For a used Forester the choice is simple: 2016–2018 or 2021 onward.

honda/odyssey.note: The fourth-generation Odyssey (2011–2017) is one of the best minivans in the dataset, scoring in the 70s and 80s. The fifth generation launched for 2018 with a ten-speed automatic and a new infotainment system, and the record collapsed: nearly a thousand complaints for each of 2018 and 2019, most of them transmission shudder and hesitation, sliding-door failures, and the rear-seat entertainment system. The 2021–2024 years recover to the 60s. The 2025 model year has jumped again, with idle stop-start failures and unintended braking cited in the owner reports quoted on its page. The 2014–2017 cars remain the safest used buy.

toyota/rav4.note: The RAV4 is consistent through the fourth generation (2013–2018), scoring between 76 and 88 every year. The fifth generation launched for 2019 with a new eight-speed automatic and a direct-injection 2.5-litre engine, and the 2019–2020 years carry the highest counts in the nameplate's history: transmission hesitation and lurching at low speed, fuel-tank capacity shortfalls, and coolant leaks from the engine block on early 2019–2020 engines that led to a warranty extension. The 2021–2023 years improve. The RAV4 Hybrid has a separate record and is generally quieter than the petrol car.

dodge/durango.note: The third-generation Durango launched for 2011 on the Grand Cherokee's platform and inherited its early electrical problems — the Totally Integrated Power Module, the alternator recall, and the Pentastar V6 cylinder-head failure. The 2011–2014 years score in the 20s and 30s. From 2016, once the eight-speed and the electrical fixes had been in production for two years, the Durango becomes one of the better large SUVs on the site, and the 2020 and 2023–2025 years score above 90.

hyundai/santa-fe.note: The Santa Fe carries the Theta II 2.4 and 2.0 turbo engines and the same recall history as the Sonata, but its complaint counts are lower because its volumes are lower. The 2017 model year is the outlier, with 951 complaints, almost all engine failure and fire. The 2018–2020 years score in the 80s. The fifth generation launched for 2024 with a new look and a new platform, and its first two years are following the launch-year pattern seen across Hyundai: electrical, infotainment and transmission complaints, and scores in the 30s and 40s so far.

chevrolet/traverse.note: The first-generation Traverse (2009–2017) carries timing-chain and engine complaints on the 3.6-litre V6, plus the steering-rack and power-steering complaints of the 2011–2014 years. The 2015–2017 cars score in the 70s. The second generation from 2018 has a moderate record with the 2021–2023 years above 85. The third generation launched for 2024 with a 2.5-litre turbo four-cylinder replacing the V6; the 2025 year is following the usual launch pattern with a spike in electrical and transmission complaints.

gmc/acadia.note: The Acadia is the Traverse's sibling, and its record has the same first-generation timing-chain and steering complaints, with the 2014 year the worst. The second generation launched for 2017 on a smaller platform with a new transmission, and that year has 1,340 complaints, most of them the shift-to-park fault in which the vehicle cannot recognise that the shifter is in Park; General Motors extended the warranty on the shifter after a class action. The 2020–2024 years score in the 80s.

chrysler/200.note: The second-generation 200 launched for 2015 with the ZF nine-speed automatic and a rotary shifter, and that single model year carries nearly 2,000 complaints, most of them the transmission: harsh shifts, loss of drive, and shutdowns. Chrysler recalled the car twice for transmission software and wiring. The 2016 and 2017 years, with revised software, score 78 and 92 — but by then the model was ending; Chrysler discontinued the 200 in 2017. The 2011–2014 first generation is a different, older car with a moderate record.

dodge/grand-caravan.note: The fifth-generation Grand Caravan ran from 2008 to 2020 with few changes, and its record is steady — transmission and electrical complaints at a moderate level, scoring in the 70s and 80s — apart from the 2016 model year, which carries 1,155 complaints for reasons the record attributes mainly to the six-speed transmission and the air-conditioning system. The 2017–2020 years are among the cheapest reliable people-carriers on the site.

chevrolet/cruze.note: The first-generation Cruze (2011–2015) carries the 1.4-litre turbo's coolant-leak, water-pump and turbocharger complaints, plus the six-speed automatic's shudder; the 2012 and 2014 years are the worst. The second generation from 2016 is a better car in the data, with the 2017–2019 years scoring 86 to 93. The diesel Cruze has a small separate record. Chevrolet ended the Cruze in 2019.

toyota/camry.note: The Camry's reputation for invulnerability is only partly borne out by the record. The 2007–2011 cars with the 2.4-litre engine consumed oil and had melting dashboards; the 2011–2012 years carry those complaints. The 2013–2017 seventh generation is quiet, with the 2014 car scoring 93. The eighth generation launched for 2018 with a new 2.5-litre engine and eight-speed automatic, and the 2018 year carries 734 complaints — transmission hesitation at low speed and the infotainment system — with 2019 not much better. From 2021 the counts fall and the 2022–2024 cars score in the 80s. The Camry Hybrid is consistently quieter than the petrol car.

chrysler/pacifica.note: The Pacifica launched for 2017 with the nine-speed automatic and a new electrical architecture, and its first year carries nearly 1,500 complaints: stalling, the transmission, the sliding doors, the Uconnect screen and, on the plug-in hybrid, a recall for fire risk. The 2018 year is only somewhat better. The 2019–2020 cars score 70 and 80, and the 2022–2025 years are moderate. The plug-in hybrid has its own recall history and should be checked separately at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

volkswagen/jetta.note: The sixth-generation Jetta (2011–2018) opened with a cheapened interior and a cluster of engine and electrical complaints; the 2011–2013 years score in the 20s and 30s. The diesel versions are the cars affected by the emissions scandal and the buy-back. From 2014 the record improves steadily and the 2018 year scores 87. The seventh generation launched for 2019 with a new platform, a 1.4-litre turbo and an eight-speed automatic, and the first year spikes again before the 2020–2024 years settle in the 80s.

toyota/corolla.note: The Corolla's record is as flat as its reputation suggests, with two dips. The 2009–2011 cars carry the same oil-consumption and steering complaints as the Camry of the period. The 2020 model year, the first of the twelfth generation with a new continuously variable transmission and a new infotainment system, doubles the complaint count and scores 45; the counts fall again from 2021. The 2013–2018 cars score between 78 and 86 and are among the cheapest reliable compact cars on the site. The Corolla Hybrid from 2020 has a separate record.

jeep/compass.note: The second-generation Compass launched for 2018 with the nine-speed automatic and the 2.4-litre Tigershark engine, and that year carries 933 complaints — the transmission, the engine stalling and consuming oil, and the electrical system. Jeep revised the transmission software and, in 2022, the engine-control calibration; the 2020–2021 years score in the 80s and 90s. The 2022 facelift year dips again, and 2023 onward recovers. The first-generation Compass (2007–2017) has a low, steady record.

ford/mustang.note: The Mustang's record is moderate and steady through the fifth generation (2005–2014). The sixth generation launched for 2015 with the 2.3-litre EcoBoost engine and independent rear suspension, and the 2015 year carries the highest count of the modern car — the EcoBoost's head-gasket and coolant complaints, and the six-speed automatic. Counts fall from 2017 and the 2018–2022 cars score in the 70s and 80s. The seventh generation from 2024 has a small record so far.

nissan/sentra.note: The seventh-generation Sentra (2013–2019) shares the Altima's CVT problem, and the 2013 model year carries 638 complaints, most of them transmission shudder, overheating and failure. Nissan extended the CVT warranty on these cars. From 2015 the counts fall steadily, and the eighth generation from 2020 scores in the 70s and 80s, with the 2023 car at 92.

dodge/charger.note: The seventh-generation Charger launched for 2011, and its first two years carry the highest counts in the nameplate's run — the Totally Integrated Power Module and alternator failures shared with the Grand Cherokee and Durango of the same years, plus the five-speed automatic. From 2015, with the eight-speed automatic and the revised electrical system, the record is quiet: the 2020–2023 years score between 88 and 92, which is unusual for a large performance saloon.

gmc/terrain.note: The Terrain's record is one of the more consistent in the dataset. The first generation (2010–2017) carries the 2.4-litre oil-consumption and timing-chain complaints shared with the Equinox, but at a moderate level, and the 2016–2017 years score above 90. The second generation from 2018 opened with a modest bump for the shift-to-park fault and has scored between 72 and 93 since. There is no year of the Terrain in the data that stands out as one to avoid.

dodge/journey.note: The Journey ran from 2009 to 2020 with the same basic platform, and its record is moderate throughout — brake wear, the four-speed automatic on the base four-cylinder, and the electrical system. The 2015 year carries the most complaints; the 2017–2020 years score between 71 and 93 and are among the cheapest three-row vehicles on the site to buy, if not to run.

toyota/prius.note: The third-generation Prius (2010–2015) carries complaints about the inverter, the brake actuator, and, on the 2010–2011 cars, oil consumption and head-gasket failure on the 1.8-litre engine. Hybrid-battery degradation on high-mileage examples appears as complaints rather than recalls. The 2012–2015 years score above 75. The fourth generation from 2016 is quiet. MotorJury carries battery-warranty and replacement-cost figures for every Prius year.

tesla/model-s.note: The early Model S (2012–2015) carries complaints about the drive unit, the retractable door handles, the touchscreen's eMMC memory chip wearing out — the subject of a 2021 recall — and the suspension. Later years shift toward Autopilot and touchscreen complaints. The record is unusual in that the most complained-about component is software, not mechanical. MotorJury carries battery-warranty and replacement-cost figures for every Tesla year.

tesla/model-3.note: The Model 3's 2018 launch year carries the highest count of the nameplate — paint and panel-fit complaints, the touchscreen, phantom braking under Autopilot, and delivery-quality issues — and the counts fall in every subsequent year. The 2021 onward cars have a moderate record dominated by driver-assistance complaints. The heat-pump failure on 2021–2022 cars in cold climates was addressed by a recall.

ford/f-150.note: The F-150's record is spread thin across an enormous volume, which is why its scores are better than its complaint counts suggest. The 2011–2014 trucks carry the first-generation 3.5-litre EcoBoost's timing-chain and condensation complaints. The aluminium-bodied 2015 year adds transmission and electrical complaints at launch. The ten-speed automatic from 2017 carries shudder and harsh-shift complaints. The 2021 fourteenth generation opened with the usual launch-year spike, including the PowerBoost hybrid's software. There is no catastrophic year; there are launch years to skip.

chevrolet/silverado-1500.note: The Silverado 1500's record follows its generations: the 2014 launch of the K2XX truck brought the eight-speed automatic's shudder and the 5.3-litre's cylinder-deactivation lifter complaints; the 2019 launch of the T1 truck brought a spike in electrical and transmission complaints. The lifter problem on the 5.3 and 6.2 V8s from 2019 onward has been the subject of a federal investigation. Between the launch years the truck scores respectably for its volume.

ford/fusion-hybrid.note: The Fusion Hybrid's scores are all BUY, from 80 for the 2011 to 90 for the 2014, but the 2011 and 2012 cars carry 2,869 and 2,557 owner complaints, almost the same as the petrol Fusion of those years, and I would walk past them. The 2013, at 84 on 1,861 complaints, is the year to buy and the last with a full record; from 2014 the Hybrid has no complaints on file and the 2016 to 2020 cars are DATA PENDING. Steering leads every scored year, at 1,436 in 2011, 1,464 in 2012 and 398 in 2013, and the petrol Fusion's steering campaign, 15V340000, covers 2011 and 2012 Fusions without the 3.5-litre engine. Air Bags is second in 2011 and 2012 at 364 and 434. The Hybrid's own page carries two campaigns, 14V736000 for a transmission control module on 2015 cars and 18V592000 for the plug-in Energi charge cord. EPA combined economy runs from 38 miles per gallon for 2011 to 42 from 2017.

ford/edge.note: Avoid the 2013 Edge, which scores 42 on 2,442 owner complaints, and the 2017, which scores 35 on 1,314, the lowest of the fourteen years on record. Buy a 2014, which scores 85 on 381 complaints, or a 2020 to 2024, which score between 82 and 90 with no year above 312 complaints. The first generation's problem is Electrical System and Service Brakes, at 852 and 634 on the 2013 and 686 and 309 on the 2011, with no recall campaign behind either category. The second generation, from 2015, swaps that for Engine, which leads at 188, 310, 658 and 431 through 2018, with Engine And Engine Cooling alongside it at 259 on the 2017; the campaigns on those years are for brake hoses (20V469000, 25V544000) and torque converter welds on 2.0-litre cars (17V427000, 18V390000). The 2019 facelift shifts the load to Power Train at 448, covered by 20V550000, and the 2021 onward scores rest on counts of 128 or fewer.

ford/taurus.note: Avoid the 2013, 2014 and 2015 Taurus, which score 31, 45 and 37 on 589, 234 and 269 owner complaints. Buy a 2016 to 2019, which score 83, 86, 85 and 93 on 80 or fewer complaints each, or a 2012 at 82, and accept that those scores rest on medium or low evidence. The 2013 facelift is where the record turns: Steering accounts for 296 of that year's 589 complaints and Fuel/Propulsion System for 98, and the campaigns match, with 15V340000 for the electric power assist steering on 2011 to 2013 cars, 13V227000 and 15V812000 for a cracking fuel delivery module and 16V621000 for the fuel pump on 3.5-litre turbocharged cars. Steering stays first on the 2014 at 67, and the 2015 adds Back Over Prevention at 52, covered by the rearview camera campaign 25V695000 on 2015 to 2019 cars. From 2016 no component reaches 26 in any year, and the 2016 has four campaigns with none safety-critical.

ford/flex.note: Avoid the 2013 Flex, which scores 34 on 578 owner complaints, and the 2019, the final year, which scores 42 on 240 complaints with 134 of them for the rearview camera. Buy a 2015 to 2018, which score 79, 83, 91 and 87 on 105 or fewer complaints each, or a 2011 or 2012 at 81 and 89. The 2013 facelift brought the same trouble as the Taurus built alongside it: Electrical System leads at 200 and Steering follows at 149, with 15V340000 covering the electric power assist steering and 13V227000 and 15V812000 a fuel delivery module that may crack. The 2014 is CAUTION at 51 on 249, still led by Steering at 66. The middle years are quiet, with no safety-critical campaign on the 2016, 2017 or 2018. The 2019's camera count has two campaigns behind it, 24V951000 and 25V695000, and 18V548000 covers unsecured starter and alternator cables on the same year.

ford/bronco.note: No Bronco year is AVOID, but the 2022 and 2023 are CAUTION at 51 and 60 on 369 and 218 owner complaints, and the 2022's rate of 92.2 complaints per year on the road is more than double the 2021's 45.0. Buy a 2021, which scores 71 on 225 complaints, or a 2024 at 76 on 74, and check the recall history, because every Bronco year has twelve campaigns. Engine leads the 2021 at 68, and 24V635000 covers 2021 and 2022 trucks with the 2.7-litre engine whose intake valves may break. Visibility/Wiper leads the 2022 at 65 and the 2023 at 89, matching 22V451000 for a windscreen that may not have been bonded properly and 24V142000 for rear quarter glass that can detach from the hard top. The 2024 and 2025 carry three separate campaigns for front control arm fasteners. The 2025 has no complaints on file yet and its score of 73 rests on low evidence.

ford/bronco-sport.note: Avoid the 2021 Bronco Sport, which scores 33 on 678 owner complaints and 135.6 complaints for every year on the road, with twelve recall campaigns of which six are safety-critical. Buy a 2024, which scores 73 on 103 complaints, the first year the record marks BUY; the 2022 and 2023 are CAUTION at 54 and 65. The 2021's complaints spread across Electrical System (205), Power Train (176), Engine (141) and Service Brakes (127), and each category has a campaign: 24V267000 and 25V019000 for a 12-volt battery that can fail without the control modules noticing, 21V011000 for a rear drive unit that may seize, 22V859000 and its follow-ups for a fuel injector on 1.5-litre engines that may crack and leak, and 21V922000 for rear brake linings made incorrectly. The 2022 carries eight safety-critical campaigns, the most of any year, and Engine (78) and Electrical System (73) still lead it. By 2024 the leading categories are down to 26 and 22.

ford/ecosport.note: Every EcoSport year is BUY, from 70 for the 2018 to 93 for the 2022, and the trend runs the right way: 723 owner complaints and 90.4 per year on the road for the 2018, then 457, 393 and 257 for 2019 to 2021, and 10 for the 2022. The 2019 to 2021 cars, at 80, 77 and 84, are the ones to buy, provided the oil pump belt campaign has been done. The record is two categories deep: Engine and Engine And Engine Cooling are 353 and 311 on the 2018 and 84 and 134 on the 2021, and nothing else reaches 70 in any year. The campaign that matches is 23V905000, for an oil pump drive belt or tensioner that may fail and cause a loss of oil pressure on every EcoSport from 2018 to 2022. The only safety-critical campaign is 20V791000, for an air bag module missing propellant on the 2020, and 25V126000 covers front half shafts that may disconnect on 2021 and 2022 cars.

ford/expedition.note: Avoid the 2019 and 2020 Expedition, which score 42 and 41 on 481 and 397 owner complaints, both led by Power Train at 211 and 252. Buy a 2015, which scores 89 on 164 complaints with no safety-critical campaign, or a 2023 to 2025, which score 79, 73 and 73 on 71 or fewer complaints each; the 2018, 2021 and 2022 are CAUTION at 55, 63 and 65. The 2018 redesign brought the ten-speed automatic, and the campaigns follow it: 18V213000 for a roll pin that may not have been installed, 20V263000 for a not-in-Park warning that is too short on the 2019, and 26V402000 for a park pawl that may engage while moving on 2018 to 2021 trucks. Seat Belts is third on the 2019 at 90, with 24V099000, 25V197000 and 26V344000 for a front pretensioner that can lock on its own. The 2017 scores 74 with Service Brakes at 77, covered by 22V150000 for a master cylinder that can leak into the booster.

chevrolet/tahoe.note: Avoid the 2021 Tahoe, the first year of the current generation, which scores 39 on 443 owner complaints and carries twelve recall campaigns, ten of them safety-critical. Buy a 2022, 2024 or 2025, which score 77, 82 and 82 on 182, 62 and 46 complaints; the 2023 is CAUTION at 61 on 209. The 2021's record is Engine at 162, Fuel/Propulsion System 93, Power Train 86 and Electrical System 56, and its campaigns cover a fuel tank missing adhesive between its layers (21V064000), a fuel pump control module that can stop the pump (21V739000), software that can cut power steering assist (21V455000), brake systems calibrated incorrectly by dealers (21V579000) and four separate seat belt faults. Engine leads every year after, at 69, 111, 21 and 26, and 25V274000 covers the 6.2-litre eight-cylinder engine on 2021 to 2024 trucks for a connecting rod or crankshaft that may fail. The 2024 and 2025 scores rest on medium and low evidence.

gmc/yukon.note: No Yukon year is AVOID, but the 2021 and 2024 are CAUTION at 60 and 68, on 312 and 166 owner complaints, and the 2024's rate of 83.0 complaints per year on the road is the highest of the five years. Buy a 2022 or 2025, which score 81 and 83 on 173 and 52 complaints; the 2023 is BUY at 72 on 223, though its rate of 74.3 per year is above the 2021's 62.4. Engine is the leading category in every year, at 169, 104, 144, 118 and 34, and the campaign that speaks to it is 25V274000, for a connecting rod or crankshaft that may fail on 2021 to 2024 trucks with the 6.2-litre eight-cylinder engine. The 2021 shares the Tahoe's launch-year campaigns, twelve in all with eight safety-critical, among them 21V064000 for a fuel tank missing adhesive and 21V455000 for a loss of power steering assist. After 2021 the recall count falls to five, four, three and two.

cadillac/escalade.note: Avoid the 2023 Escalade, which scores 42 on 133 owner complaints, 103 of them for the Engine, and treat the 2021, 2022 and 2024 as CAUTION at 52, 58 and 60. Buy a 2018, 2019 or 2020, which score 93, 95 and 91 on 21, 25 and 14 complaints, or a 2011 to 2014 at 81 to 91, all on low evidence. The current generation, from 2021, is the problem: Engine leads at 46, 63, 103 and 32 through 2024, and 25V274000 covers the 6.2-litre eight-cylinder engine on 2021 to 2024 trucks for a connecting rod or crankshaft that may fail. The 2021 also carries nine campaigns, five safety-critical, most shared with the Tahoe and Yukon. The 2015 redesign is CAUTION at 67 on 103 complaints with seven safety-critical campaigns, including 19V645000 for a brake vacuum pump. Its complaints per year of exposure are lower than the Expedition, Tahoe or Yukon in every year from 2021 except 2023, but its evidence is medium or low throughout.

toyota/highlander.note: Avoid the 2018 to 2020 Highlander, which score 46, 40 and 37 on 261, 472 and 306 complaints, and treat the 2017 at 57 as a car that needs its drivetrain history documented. Buy a 2011 to 2016, where every year scores between 78 and 86 and none has more than 210 complaints. The split is the 2017 facelift: Power Train, which had 8 complaints on the 2014, becomes the top component at 71 on the 2017, 62 on the 2018, 188 on the 2019 and 120 on the 2020. The 2019 adds Fuel/Propulsion System at 86 and two safety-critical fuel pump campaigns, 20V012000 and 20V682000, covering 2017 to 2019. The 2020 is a new generation with the same Power Train pattern, an engine control unit campaign for the 3.5-litre V6 (20V162000) and two air bag campaigns. The 2021 to 2024 cars have no complaints on record, so no verdict is possible. Steering leads the 2011 to 2013 at 34, 47 and 46, but nothing on those years recurs.

toyota/highlander-hybrid.note: Avoid the 2017 Highlander Hybrid, which scores 47 on 224 complaints, and treat the 2015 and 2016 as CAUTION years at 50 and 51 on 182 and 108. Buy a 2018 to 2020, which score 94, 93 and 83 on 5, 6 and 9 complaints, or a 2022 at 87, all with low evidence. The hybrid's 540 complaints sit almost entirely in 2015 to 2017, and in those years its component pattern is nearly identical to the petrol Highlander's: Electrical System 48 and Unknown Or Other 41 on the 2015 against 52 and 43 for the petrol car, and Power Train 45, Engine 42 and Service Brakes 29 on the 2017 against the petrol car's 71, 45 and 29. Read those three years as the petrol car's record rather than a separate hybrid fault. The 2015 to 2017 hybrids carry no safety-critical recalls; the 2020 shares the petrol car's air bag campaigns 20V633000 and 23V865000. Fuel economy is 28 mpg combined through 2019 and 36 from 2020.

toyota/tacoma.note: Avoid the 2016, 2017 and 2019 Tacoma (323, 239 and 217 complaints, scores of 55, 61 and 54) and the 2024 and 2025 fourth-generation trucks, which score 38 each at 72.5 and 86.0 complaints per year on the road, the highest rates on record. Buy a 2013 to 2015, scoring 85, 90 and 89 on 124, 93 and 101 complaints, or a 2020 to 2023, all at 76 or better on 87 complaints or fewer. The third generation launched for 2016 and Power Train went from 13 complaints on the 2014 to 136, with campaigns 17V285000 for rear differential oil leaks and 17V356000 for a crank position sensor that can stall six-cylinder trucks. The 2019 is a brake and fuel year, Service Brakes 56 and Fuel/Propulsion System 55, with 18V888000 for the brake master cylinder and fuel pump campaigns 20V012000 and 20V682000. The 2024 has Power Train 52 and Service Brakes 34. The 2012 is a CAUTION at 67 on 122 Engine complaints with no campaign to close them.

toyota/sienna.note: Avoid the 2011 Sienna, which scores 28 on 612 complaints, 211 of them Air Bags and 154 Structure, with twelve recall campaigns. Buy a 2018 to 2020, which score 76, 77 and 88 on 69, 45 and 38 complaints, or the 2016 at 83 on 75. The third generation opened badly and improved slowly: the 2012 (247 complaints) and 2015 (230) are CAUTION years, and the 2013 and 2014 sit at 69 and 72. Air Bags is the passenger-side inflator module campaigns, four of which touch the 2011 alone, and Structure is the power sliding door campaign 16V858000, which covers every van from 2011 to 2016 and is why Structure leads the component table in each of those years. The 2017 changes shape: Power Train leads at 36, and the year carries ten campaigns, six safety-critical, including 18V211000 for the brake vacuum pump and the fuel pump campaigns 20V012000 and 20V682000 that run to 2020. The 2022 to 2025 vans have no complaints on record.

toyota/4runner.note: Avoid the 2025 4Runner, the first year of a new generation, which scores 44 on 56 complaints at 56.0 per year on the road, with Service Brakes at 23. Buy a 2017 (89 on 36 complaints) or any year from 2020 to 2024, which score between 79 and 90 on 39 complaints or fewer. The 4Runner's 817 complaints make it the quietest of the Toyota trucks, and its only other weak year is the 2011, a CAUTION at 57 where 112 of 163 complaints are Air Bags, matched by six inflator module and sensor campaigns reaching 2011 to 2015 cars. The 2012 has 70 Air Bags complaints out of 96 and five safety-critical recalls, the most of any year. From 2013 no year exceeds 85 complaints. Steering at 11 on the 2018 and 10 on the 2019 matches campaign 19V670000 for distributor-fitted steering parts that may not have been tightened; both years are inside the 20V682000 fuel pump campaign.

toyota/tundra.note: Avoid the 2023 Tundra, which scores 32 on 394 complaints at 131.3 per year on the road, with Engine at 161, Power Train at 83 and Fuel/Propulsion System at 60. Buy a 2013 to 2015, which score 81, 79 and 86 on 84, 92 and 48 complaints, or the 2020 at 78 on 45. The second generation has three phases: Engine leads the 2011 to 2013 at 35, 57 and 23 without an engine campaign on file; the 2014 and 2015 are quiet; and the 2016 to 2019 are electrical years, with Electrical System at 26, 27, 26 and 13, Service Brakes at 34 on the 2016, and CAUTION verdicts for 2016, 2018 and 2019. Every Tundra from 2011 to 2020 is inside 21V920000 for a power steering gear that may leak oil, and the 2018 to 2020 trucks carry fuel pump campaigns 20V012000 and 20V682000. The 2023's twelve campaigns include 24V125000 for a transmission that can allow movement in neutral, but nothing on file addresses its 161 Engine complaints.

toyota/prius-c.note: No Prius c year rates AVOID; the one to be careful with is the 2013, a CAUTION at 56 on 399 complaints, 195 of them Service Brakes. Buy a 2014 or 2015, which score 81 and 89 on 205 and 132 complaints with no safety-critical recalls, or a 2018 or 2019 at 93 and 92 on 6 and 0 complaints, evidence low. The Prius c record is 742 complaints and four recall campaigns across nine model years, and its shape is the Prius shape: Service Brakes first at 195, 80 and 52 for 2013 to 2015, Electrical System second at 68, 36 and 27, then Engine and Vehicle Speed Control. There is no brake campaign on file for any year, so the brake pattern is a symptom without an official cause, and a test drive is the only check. The one substantive campaign is 19V491000 for a DC-DC converter on 2018 and 2019 cars that may fail and cause a loss of drive.

honda/civic.note: No Civic year on record rates AVOID; the one to be careful with is the 2012, a CAUTION at 68 on 454 complaints, the most of any year. Buy a 2013 or 2014, which score 84 and 82 on 316 and 290 complaints, and note that the 2013 has no recall campaigns at all. The site holds the Civic from 2011 to 2015, and the record has two halves. The 2011 to 2013 cars are air bag cars, with Air Bags the top component at 51, 149 and 112; the 2011 carries nine safety-critical campaigns, eight of them passenger-side inflator module recalls. The 2012 adds Steering at 74 and Electrical System at 59, with campaigns for a wrong steering column (12V548000) and a misaligned fuel line O-ring (11V288000). The 2014 and 2015 are transmission cars: Power Train is 98 and 175, and campaign 15V574000 covers both years for transmission control software. The 2015's 377 complaints pull it to 72, still a BUY.

honda/civic-hybrid.note: Every Civic Hybrid year on record rates BUY, with the 2012 the weakest at 73 on 455 complaints and the 2013 and 2014 the best at 84 and 85 on 310 and 282. Buy a 2013 or 2014; neither carries a recall campaign. The record runs from 2011 to 2015 and totals 1,578 complaints, and it is the petrol Civic's record within a few complaints in every year: 166 against 168 in 2011, 455 against 454 in 2012, 365 against 377 in 2015. The components match too. Air Bags leads the 2011 to 2013 at 49, 146 and 106, Steering is 73 on the 2012, and Power Train takes over on the 2014 and 2015 at 95 and 169, so the hybrid shares the Civic's transmission pattern even though the transmission software campaign 15V574000 is filed against the petrol car. The 2011 has six safety-critical campaigns, all passenger-side inflator module recalls; the 2012 has one, 20V770000, for a driveshaft on manual cars. Fuel economy is 41 to 44 mpg combined.

honda/fit.note: The Fit years to walk past are the 2015 and 2019, both CAUTION verdicts, at 52 on 282 complaints and 60 on 134. Buy a 2016 or 2020, which score 86 each on 119 and 35 complaints, or a 2018 at 75. The record runs from 2011 to 2020 with no 2014 and no complaints on the 2017. The 2011 to 2013 cars are air bag years: Air Bags is 64, 41 and 92, and the 2011 and 2012 carry eleven campaigns each, ten and nine of them safety-critical, nearly all inflator module recalls. The 2015 opened the third generation with Electrical System at 115, Fuel/Propulsion System 41, Engine 40 and Power Train 38; its campaigns are 15V559000 for ignition coils and 15V574000 for transmission control software. The 2019 repeats the electrical and fuel pattern at 47 and 40, with three fuel pump campaigns, 20V314000, 21V215000 and 23V858000, the last also covering the 2018. Every 2018 to 2020 Fit is inside 23V046000 for a rearview camera that may not display.

honda/hr-v.note: Avoid the 2023 and 2024 HR-V, which score 37 and 47; the 2023 has 685 complaints at 228.3 per year on the road, the highest rate in the nameplate's record, with Visibility/Wiper at 319 and Steering at 77. Buy a 2017 (92 on 121 complaints), a 2020 or 2021 (81 and 85), or a 2016 or 2018 at 79 each. The first generation from 2016 to 2022 has one weak year, the 2019, a CAUTION at 56 on 230 complaints with Electrical System 66 and seven recall campaigns, five safety-critical, including three fuel pump campaigns (20V314000, 21V215000, 23V858000) and 18V777000 for rear brake caliper pistons. The second generation launched for 2023 and the record turned at once. There is no campaign on file for the 319 visibility complaints; Steering has one, 24V744000, safety-critical, covering 2023 to 2025. The 2024 has Steering top at 51 with two seat cushion frame campaigns. The 2025 has 42 complaints, Steering at 13, and a CAUTION at 68 with low evidence.

acura/mdx.note: Avoid the 2016 to 2020 MDX, where the 2016 scores 49 on 367 complaints and the 2020 scores 47 on 215, with the 2017 to 2019 CAUTION at 58, 66 and 59, and avoid the 2025 at 39 on 94 complaints in its first year. Buy a 2011 to 2013, which score 95, 92 and 94 on 70, 76 and 29 complaints, or a 2015 at 80. Engine is the top component on every MDX from 2016 to 2020, at 157, 78, 35, 46 and 79, and a late campaign explains it: 23V751000, issued in November 2023, covers 2016 to 2020 cars for a connecting rod bearing that may wear because of a manufacturing error. Power Train is 111 on the 2016, the year the nine-speed automatic arrived, and 64 on the 2017. Fuel pump campaigns 19V060000, 23V858000 and 21V215000 also cover these years, and the 2020 carries five safety-critical recalls, the most of any year. The 2023 and 2024 score 85 and 79 on 38 complaints each, evidence low.

acura/rdx.note: Avoid the 2019 and 2020 RDX, which score 32 each on 433 and 344 complaints, and the 2015 at 39 on 409, with the 2014 (50) and 2021 (51) as CAUTION years to walk past. Buy a 2016 to 2018, which score 89, 88 and 84 on 40, 75 and 77 complaints, or a 2022 to 2024 at 83 to 84 on 31, 21 and 11. The 2013 to 2015 second-generation cars complain about Exterior Lighting, at 89, 162 and 337, more than four fifths of the 2015's total, with no lighting campaign on file; Air Bags is second at 36, 41 and 33, matching the driver-side inflator module campaigns 16V061000 and 19V182000. The third generation launched for 2019 with Unknown Or Other at 139, Visibility/Wiper at 96 and Engine at 89, and five safety-critical recalls on each of the 2019 and 2020, including fuel pump campaigns 21V215000 and 23V858000. The 2025 is a CAUTION at 58 with Steering at 23, matched by 25V582000 for power steering software.

acura/tlx.note: Avoid the 2015 TLX, the nameplate's first year, which scores 38 on 341 complaints with Power Train at 160 and Engine at 82. Buy a 2016 or 2017, which score 78 and 84 on 110 and 70 complaints, or a 2022 to 2025, which score 85, 84, 89 and 87 on 25, 10, 5 and 4 complaints, evidence low. The 2015 carries two transmission campaigns specific to it, 14V779000 for the automatic transmission on V6 cars and 16V640000 for wire harness crimps that can cause an unexpected shift, and it is the first year of 23V751000, the connecting rod bearing campaign that runs to 2020, and of 19V060000, the V6 fuel pump campaign. From 2016 the counts are small, and Engine is the top component each year from 2016 to 2020 at 27, 23, 30, 31 and 19. The 2019 and 2021 are CAUTION at 67 and 69; the 2021 has Power Train 26 with 24V950000 for a fuel filler neck weld and 25V391000 for the brake pedal pivot pin.

bmw/3-series.note: Avoid the 2011 3 Series, which has 994 owner complaints and a score of 31, and the 2014 car, with 555 complaints and a score of 36. Buy the 2013 car, 74 complaints and a score of 87, or the 2012 at 78 on 177. The 2011 record is led by Engine at 312, Air Bags at 214 and Electrical System at 202, and its eight recall campaigns include the engine (14V176000), the crankcase ventilation heater (17V683000) and two driver air bag inflators, 20V017000 and 24V513000. The 2014 car adds a fuel problem to an engine one: Fuel/Propulsion System at 112 and Fuel System at 50 sit beside 15V189000 for the petrol fuel pump and, on the 328d, 21V586000 for the high-pressure diesel pump, and the year carries 11 campaigns, eight safety-critical. The 2015 car is CAUTION at 56 on 363 complaints, with Electrical System at 130. From 2016 the table shows no complaints and low evidence, so the BUY scores of 72 to 86 are provisional.

bmw/5-series.note: Avoid the 2011 5 Series, with 1,063 owner complaints and a score of 37, and the 2012 car, with 317 complaints and a score of 46. No 5 Series year with a deep record does better than CAUTION: the 2013 and 2014 cars score 58 and 54 on 252 and 233 complaints, and the 2017 to 2019 cars that score 91 to 94 do so on 18, 0 and 12 complaints with low evidence. The 2011 car is unusual in that Tires is its top component at 235, ahead of Engine at 210, Power Train at 159, Fuel/Propulsion System at 133 and Steering at 117, and none of its six campaigns addresses tyres or steering; they cover the engine (14V176000), the 550i turbocharger (18V248000), the fuel pump (16V746000) and an air bag sensor cluster (16V832000). Recall activity rises again on the 2020 and 2021 cars, with 21V046000 for output shafts on xDrive models and 26V525000 for the driveshaft on 540i and M550i cars.

bmw/x3.note: Avoid the 2013 X3, which has 452 owner complaints and a score of 56, and the 2015 car, with 420 complaints and a score of 51. Buy the 2012 car, 96 complaints and a score of 94, then the 2014 at 89 on 172 or the 2011 at 85 on 250. The record stops there: the X3 has no recall campaigns on record in any year and nothing scored from 2016 onward, where every year reads DATA PENDING. The 2013 car's problem is the engine, with Engine at 294 complaints against 22 for the 2012 car, and Power Train second at 120. The 2015 car has Engine at 116, Electrical System at 88 and Engine And Engine Cooling at 60, and at 38.2 complaints per year on the road it is the worst X3 on the site's normalising measure. Because no campaign exists to point at, the engine service history is the whole inspection on a 2013 or 2015 car.

bmw/x5.note: The X5 scores BUY in every year the record covers, 2011 to 2015, between 80 and 90, and nothing from 2016 onward is scored. The 2013 and 2014 cars are the ones to buy, scoring 90 on 483 and 392 complaints, while the 2012 car, at 813 complaints and 58.1 per year on the road, is the year to look at hardest. Engine is the top component in 2011, 2012 and 2015, at 330, 276 and 168, and Air Bags are first or second from 2011 to 2013, at 201, 249 and 156. The 2014 car has the flattest list, with Fuel/Propulsion System at 80 ahead of Engine at 64. The 2015 car climbs back to 600 complaints, and its list adds Fuel System at 77 and Diesel at 77, so a 2015 diesel needs its fuel system inspected. No recall campaign is on record for the X5 in any year, which means the VIN lookup is the buyer's own job.

audi/q5.note: Avoid the 2018 Q5, which has 200 owner complaints and a score of 35, and the 2021 car, with 140 complaints and a score of 33. Buy a 2013 to 2017 car: complaints run 92, 106, 98, 77 and 42, scores 80, 75, 72, 78 and 87. The 2018 car's problem is electrical, with Electrical System at 69 complaints, and it carries 21V947000 for a body control module that liquid can reach from the rear seat or through a body seam, plus two brake campaigns, 18V369000 for caliper pistons and 19V277000 for a master cylinder casting. The 2021 car has Electrical System at 52 and Engine at 34, eight campaigns including 22V753000 for connecting rod bearings that may fail on 2021 to 2023 cars, and 25V080000 for the plug-in hybrid's high-voltage battery. The good years have Engine on top in modest numbers and campaigns worth checking by number: 17V001000 for sunroof drainage on every 2011 to 2017 car, and 17V298000 for a fuel pump flange that may crack.

audi/q7.note: Avoid the 2017 Q7, which has 319 owner complaints and a score of 29, the 2018 car at 43 on 141 complaints, and the 2021 car at 31 on 71. Buy a 2011 to 2015 car, which scores 86 to 88 on 23 to 45 complaints a year, though with evidence the site marks low, or the 2020 at 79 on 26 complaints. The 2017 car was the first of a new generation and its top component is Exterior Lighting at 133, which no campaign on record addresses, followed by Engine at 60 and Electrical System at 53. Its seven campaigns, six safety-critical, include 16V519000 for an air bag control module, 16V648000 for the electric power steering control unit, 19V035000 for leaking fuel rails and 20V149000 for a steering shaft bolt that may loosen on 2017 to 2019 cars. The 2021 car has Electrical System at 43 and nine campaigns, including 25V201000 for an instrument panel display that may fail.

porsche/cayenne.note: Avoid the 2019 Cayenne, which has 67 owner complaints and a score of 40, and the 2020 car, with 69 complaints and a score of 42. Buy a 2012, 2014, 2015, 2017 or 2018 car, which score 92 to 95 on 28 complaints or fewer, or a 2022 to 2024 car. The 2019 car was the first of a new generation and carries seven recall campaigns, the most in the table, two of them for the instrument cluster, 19V115000 and 19V735000, which sit under Electrical System at 19, the year's top component; 18V751000 covers a rear seat belt buckle that may break and 20V270000 a fuel line connector that may leak on Turbo models. The 2020 car adds 20V271000 for a transmission oil pipe weld, and the 2021 car, CAUTION at 59, has 21V493000 for a steering column connection that may fail. The 2011 car, CAUTION at 59 on 106 complaints, has Engine at 54 and 17V368000 for camshaft controllers on S and Turbo models.

infiniti/q50.note: Avoid the 2014 Q50, which has 169 owner complaints and a score of 37, and the 2015 car, with 125 complaints and a score of 44. Buy a 2016 or newer car: complaints fall to 39, then 62, 42, 30 and 3 through 2020, with scores of 79, 66, 79, 87 and 94. The 2014 car's problem is steering, with Steering at 78 complaints, more than the next three components together, and two safety-critical campaigns name it: 13V588000 for Direct Adaptive Steering software and 16V430000 for the same system on 2014 to 2016 cars. The 2015 car shifts to Power Train at 39 with Steering second at 28. A later campaign, 24V470000, covers a driveshaft that can fatigue and break on 2014 to 2018 two-wheel-drive cars. The 2017 car is CAUTION at 66, with 17V476000 for fuel pump control module software on 2016 to 2018 2.0-litre cars. From 2016 Engine is the top component, at 10 to 17 a year, and Steering leaves the top five after 2016.

infiniti/qx60.note: Avoid the 2014 QX60, which has 229 owner complaints and a score of 33. Buy a 2015 or newer car: the 2015 scores 76 on 92 complaints, the 2016 scores 93 on 29, and every year from 2018 to 2020 is at 88 or better on 38 complaints or fewer. The 2014 car's problem is the power train, with Power Train at 118 complaints, more than half the year's total, and no campaign on record addresses it, so the remedy has to be found in the service history. The seven campaigns it does carry, five safety-critical, cover the brakes (13V445000, 15V012000), the air bags (15V681000, 14V138000) and a wheel lug nut (14V229000). The 2017 car dips to 81 on 68 complaints, with Engine at 20, and carries 18V601000 for an anti-lock brake actuator pump that may leak onto a circuit board, and 19V807000 for cars the first repair missed. The 2022 to 2025 cars score 88, 82, 77 and 74 on low evidence, with campaigns mainly for seats.

buick/enclave.note: The Buick Enclave's year to avoid is 2014, an AVOID at 30 on 292 complaints, of which 205 are in the Air Bags category; the 2025 car is also an AVOID at 48, but on 36 complaints and low evidence. The years to buy are 2013 (83 on 69 complaints) and 2018 to 2024, where scores run from 77 to 92 on between 7 and 64 complaints a year. Air Bags stays the top component on the 2015, 2016 and 2017 cars at 105, 110 and 145, all CAUTION years; the campaigns on them include 23V334000 for a driver's air bag inflator that may explode and 21V246000 for side curtain air bags that may not be properly attached. The 2018 redesign changed the record completely: the 2018 car has 64 complaints, no recall campaigns and a score of 89. The Enclave's 1,457 complaints across fifteen years are roughly a third of the Traverse's or Acadia's, and its record from 2019 is thin.

chevrolet/impala.note: The Chevrolet Impala has one year to avoid, 2016, which carries 897 complaints, a score of 47 and no recall campaigns at all; the next highest count is 505 on the 2011 car. The years to buy are 2017 to 2020, which score 92, 91, 92 and 96 on 116, 59, 28 and 15 complaints, and the 2012 and 2013 cars, at 78 each. The 2016 complaints are spread across Engine (304), Electrical System (236), Unknown Or Other (185), Power Train (178) and Vehicle Speed Control (146), with no campaign to explain any of them; the 2015 car on the same body has 288 complaints led by Electrical System at 92, and the 2017 car has nothing above 31 in any category. The 2011 to 2013 cars are marked by the electronic stability control category (132, 54 and 108) and by campaign 14V355000, the ignition recall of 23/06/2014. The 2014 Impala has no record and is marked DATA PENDING.

buick/lacrosse.note: The Buick LaCrosse's year to avoid is 2012, an AVOID at 43 on 205 complaints, with the 2011 (51) and 2013 (57) cars either side of it both CAUTION. The years to buy are 2014 to 2019, every one a BUY with scores from 73 to 90, though complaints fall from 63 to 6 across those years and the evidence label drops to low from 2015. On the early cars Electrical System leads every year (32, 61, 54), Engine is second (30, 46, 30) and Suspension third (27, 31, 27); three campaigns, 20V764000, 21V633000 and 21V00F000, cover the rear suspension on 2010 to 2013 cars registered in northern and eastern states, and 13V173000 covers the generator control module on 2012 and 2013 cars with eAssist. The 2014 car has five campaigns, four safety-critical, but only 63 complaints. The 2017 car carries 17V116000 for electric power steering connectors that may admit water. The LaCrosse's complaint rate never exceeds 14.6 per year on the road.

dodge/challenger.note: The Dodge Challenger's year to avoid is 2012, an AVOID at 45 on 253 complaints, with 138 of them in the Electrical System category; the 2011, 2013 and 2014 cars are CAUTION at 59, 60 and 66. The years to buy are 2016 onward, where every year is a BUY and the 2020, 2021 and 2022 cars score 94, 90 and 92 on 20, 19 and 9 complaints. Electrical System is the top component on every year from 2011 to 2014 (103, 138, 104, 60), and the campaigns behind it are the alternator recalls 14V634000, 17V435000 and 17V741000 on 3.6-litre cars; Air Bags is second in 2011 and 2012 (35 and 47) with three passenger inflator campaigns. The 2015 car is a CAUTION at 67 with Power Train first at 29, and 17V431000 covers 2017 5.7-litre automatics that may not stay in Park. The 2023 car dips to 75 on 41 complaints. With 1,245 complaints in thirteen years, the Challenger has the smallest record of the three.

chrysler/300.note: The Chrysler 300's years to avoid are 2012, 2013 and 2014, all AVOID at 28, 35 and 38 on 426, 306 and 236 complaints; the 2018 car is a CAUTION at 50. The years to buy are 2015 to 2017 (76, 85, 82) and 2019 to 2023, where scores run from 81 to 91 and the 2020 and 2022 cars have 10 and 5 complaints. Electrical System leads every year from 2011 to 2014 (119, 212, 131, 72), and the campaigns on those years say why in part: the alternator recalls 14V634000, 17V435000 and 17V741000 on 3.6-litre cars, and 12V197000 for an overheated power distribution centre that can cost the 2011 and 2012 car its ABS and stability control. Power Train follows (79, 58, 69), with 16V240000 for the transmission control module. The 2018 dip brings Electrical System back to 68 and carries 18V280000 for an incorrect park lock rod; 24V198000, issued 14/03/2024, recalls 2018 to 2021 cars for side curtain air bag inflators that may rupture.

chevrolet/camaro.note: The Chevrolet Camaro has no AVOID year on record, but two to treat with caution: 2015 (score 69 on 206 complaints, with Electrical System at 111) and 2017 (62 on 185, with Steering at 57). The years to buy are 2018 (85 on 79 complaints) and 2020 to 2022 (88, 87 and 93 on 31, 16 and 13), with the 2011 and 2012 cars at 79 and 81 behind them. The fifth-generation cars are defined by campaign 14V346000, under which all 2010 to 2014 Camaros were recalled because the driver's knee could knock the ignition key out of the run position, and by an Electrical System count that grows from 81 in 2013 to 99 and then 111. The 2017 steering complaints have a documented cause: 19V086000 and 25V175000 recall the 2017 and 2018 cars because the electric power steering assist may fail. The 2020 to 2022 cars carry 25V148000, for a ten-speed automatic that may lock the wheels. The 2019, 2023 and 2024 model years have no record.

chevrolet/corvette.note: The Chevrolet Corvette's years to avoid are 2017 (AVOID at 37 on 255 complaints) and 2019 (46 on 147), and one category accounts for both: Wheels, with 223 and 124 complaints. The years to buy are 2011 and 2012 (87 and 92 on 85 and 56 complaints), 2014 and 2015 (77 and 74), and 2021 and 2022 (89 and 88 on 12 and 20). The wheel complaints have no recall campaign on any year; the campaigns on the 2017 car are for electric power steering assist that may fail (19V086000 and 25V175000) and frontal air bags, and the 2018 car has Wheels first again at 45 of 51 complaints. The 2014 and 2015 cars each carry 5 campaigns, 4 safety-critical, including the air bag sensing module and rear shock absorber welds. The 2020 car, the first mid-engine year, has 4 campaigns for the front trunk release, the seat belt retractor and the brake boost sensor, and scores 78. The 2013, 2016 and 2023 model years have no record.

cadillac/srx.note: The Cadillac SRX's year to avoid is 2015, a CAUTION at 69 on 442 complaints, of which 302 are in the Exterior Lighting category; the year to buy is 2016, the last SRX, at 88 on 168 complaints. The 2011 to 2014 cars are all BUY at 71, 81, 78 and 79, but they carry the same lighting complaint: 198, 233, 217 and 266 a year, more than half of all reports on the 2014 car. No SRX year has a lighting recall campaign, so the pattern is one owners report and the manufacturer has not been required to fix; a used SRX should be checked for headlamp condensation and dimming before anything else. Beneath it, Suspension is second on the 2011 car (62) and the rear toe link has two campaigns, 14V571000 and 21V473000, the second covering every year to 2016. The newest campaign, 26V329000 of 21/05/2026, covers the driver's air bag inflator on 2015 and 2016 cars and is likely still open.

chevrolet/sonic.note: The Chevrolet Sonic's years to avoid are 2012 (AVOID at 32 on 354 complaints) and 2013 (40 on 217); the years to buy are 2016 to 2019, which score 88, 94, 95 and 95 on 48, 37, 14 and 8 complaints. The 2014 car is a CAUTION at 60 and the 2015 car the first BUY at 70. Power Train leads the 2012 car with 154 complaints, and campaign 14V315000 covers 2012 cars with the 1.8-litre engine and six-speed automatic for a transmission defect; it is one of 7 campaigns on the 2012 car, alongside 11V599000 for a missing front brake pad and two campaigns for a shorting bar in the driver's frontal air bag. The 2013 car has 6 campaigns, all safety-critical, including 13V464000 for a fuel tank strap bracket with insufficient welds and 23V516000 for a driver's air bag inflator that may explode. Electrical System and Engine lead the 2013 and 2014 cars. From 2016 the record is thin, and the 2020 Sonic has no record at all.

chevrolet/trax.note: The Chevrolet Trax's years to avoid are the two newest, 2024 (AVOID at 44 on 169 complaints, 84.5 per year on the road) and 2025 (47 on 80); the years to buy are the first-generation cars of 2015 to 2022, every one a BUY, with 2021 and 2022 at 94 each. The first generation runs 95, 117, 111, 100, 133, 94, 24 and 9 complaints with scores from 70 to 94, and Engine is first or second in every year to 2020. Suspension leads the 2018 car at 34, and two campaigns explain it: 19V652000 and 19V312000, covering 2015 to 2019 cars whose front lower control arm joint may have been improperly welded. The 2019 car, the generation's dip at 70, also carries 18V774000 for an air bag sensing module left in manufacturing mode. The 2024 car is a different vehicle with no 2023 predecessor on record; Electrical System leads it with 64 complaints, and its single campaign, 23V744000, covers instrument display software that can blank the panel while driving.

chevrolet/blazer.note: The Chevrolet Blazer has no year to avoid on record: its lowest score is 70, on the 2020 car, and every year from 2019 to 2025 is a BUY. The years to buy are 2022 and 2023, at 92 and 90 on 49 and 42 complaints, with 2024 (86) and 2021 (81) behind them. The first two years carry the most complaints, 186 in 2019 and 213 in 2020, spread across Power Train (64 and 72), Electrical System (59 and 73) and Engine (40 and 68), and the campaigns on them are 20V668000 for the automatic transmission, 21V115000 for tyres and, on the 2020 car, 20V446000 for the roof-rail air bag diffuser. From 2021 the counts fall to 129, 49, 42, 43 and 28. The 2023 car carries 23V042000 for a half-shaft that may be missing a retaining ring and 23V172000 for a transmission built with an incorrect sun gear. Forward Collision Avoidance enters the top five from 2023 at 7, 11 and 4 complaints, not yet a pattern.

chevrolet/colorado.note: The Chevrolet Colorado's years to avoid are 2015 (AVOID at 29 on 489 complaints, 356 of them Steering) and the redesigned 2023 and 2024 trucks (46 and 40 on 131 and 121). The years to buy are 2019 to 2022, which score 81, 90, 86 and 89 on 149, 82, 73 and 51 complaints. The 2015 steering has a documented cause: campaigns 16V054000 and 21V213000 both cover a poor electrical connection in the steering gear that can cause a loss of power assist, and the 2015 truck carries 7 campaigns, 6 safety-critical, including 15V278000 for front brake calipers that may leak fluid. There is no record for the 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017 or 2018 model years. The 2023 truck's top component is Forward Collision Avoidance at 45, matched by 24V133000 for a front camera that may falsely detect an obstacle and brake; Electrical System leads the 2024 truck at 35, which also carries 24V491000 for a fuel pump lock ring. The 2025 truck scores 77 on 27 complaints.

gmc/canyon.note: The GMC Canyon's years to avoid are 2015 and 2016 (AVOID at 29 and 39, with Steering at 226 and 177 of 319 and 267 complaints) and 2023 and 2024 (45 and 39). The years to buy are 2017 to 2022, all BUY, with the 2019, 2020 and 2021 trucks at 95, 94 and 90 on 16, 14 and 11 complaints. The early steering complaints are corroborated by 16V054000 and 21V213000, both for a poor electrical connection in the steering gear that can cost the truck its power assist, and the 2015 truck's 8 campaigns, 7 safety-critical, also cover driver air bag wiring, front brake calipers and seat frame hooks. The redesigned 2023 truck has 59 complaints led by Electrical System (19) and Forward Collision Avoidance (18), the latter matched by 24V133000 for a camera that falsely triggers emergency braking. The 2024 truck is the Canyon's highest rate, 205 complaints at 102.5 per year, and 159 of them are Exterior Lighting, matched by 24V673000 for headlights that flicker.

honda/ridgeline.note: The Honda Ridgeline's only AVOID year is 2025, at 48 on 81 complaints, and its 2017, 2019, 2020 and 2023 trucks are CAUTION at 61, 60, 69 and 64. The years to buy are 2024 (85 on 54 complaints), 2022 (80 on 113) and 2021 (76 on 100). The Ridgeline's complaint counts are moderate, from 337 on the 2017 truck down to 54, but its recall counts are high, 48 campaigns with 12 on the 2019 truck alone. Electrical System leads the 2017 truck at 92, and 16V888000 covers water entering the rear wiring harness through a connector under the bed drain hole; Fuel System leads the 2019 truck at 39, and 19V053000 covers a fuel pump feed port that can crack. Engine is second on the 2017 truck at 81, and 23V751000 covers connecting rod bearings on the 2017 and 2019 trucks. From 2022 Exterior Lighting leads (30, then 39), with no matching campaign. The 2023 truck carries 24V184000 for a steering gearbox ball joint that may detach.

kia/forte.note: Avoid the 2014 Kia Forte, which has 439 complaints and a score of 44, and treat the 2012 and 2017 cars (289 and 301 complaints, scores of 67 and 52) with caution. Buy a 2018 or later car: the 2020 has 74 complaints, no recalls and a score of 90. Engine leads every bad year, with 214 of the 2014 car's complaints, 160 of the 2012 car's and 144 of the 2017 car's, and the campaigns say why: 20V750000 covers the 2012 to 2015 cars for an engine compartment fire while driving, 15V015000 covers the 2014 car for a cooling fan resistor that can overheat and melt, and 21V260000 covers the 2017 and 2018 cars for an oil pump that can fail and damage the 2.0-litre engine. The 2019 redesign changed the record: Engine drops behind Power Train in 2019 and to 17 complaints in 2020. The 2021 to 2023 cars carry steering column, steering knuckle and control arm campaigns to confirm by VIN, but their counts stay below 70.

kia/forte-koup.note: The Kia Forte Koup has no year with an AVOID verdict, but the 2014 car, with 441 complaints and a score of 56, is the one to treat with caution, and the 2016 car, with 137 complaints, no recalls and a score of 91, is the one to buy. The 2011 car (161 complaints, score 87) and the 2013 and 2015 cars (211 and 258, both scoring 78) are sound too. The two-door Koup's record moves in step with the Forte sedan's, and Engine is the top category in every scored year, at 173 on the 2012 car, 215 on the 2014 and 156 on the 2015. Campaign 20V750000 covers the 2012 to 2015 cars for an engine compartment fire while driving, 17V773000 covers the 2012 to 2014 cars for a brake pedal pad that leaves the brake lights on, and 18V363000 covers the 2011 to 2013 cars for an air bag control unit that can short circuit in a crash. The 2017 car has no complaints on record.

hyundai/veloster.note: Avoid the 2012 and 2013 Hyundai Veloster, which have 295 and 421 complaints and scores of 43 and 39, and treat the 2016 car (221 complaints, score 54) with caution. Buy a 2014 or 2015 car, which score 86 and 76, or a 2017, 2019 or 2020 car, scoring 94, 91 and 94 on small counts. Engine is the top category in every scored year, peaking at 170 on the 2013 car, where Electrical System adds 97 and Steering 58. The 2012 car's six campaigns include two for panoramic sunroof assemblies weakened at the factory and one for a parking brake that binds on manual cars; 19V204000 covers the 2013 1.6-litre turbo for engine software that can cause pre-ignition, and 20V746000 covers the 2015 and 2016 cars for connecting rod bearings that wear prematurely, the Engine count of 132 on the 2016 car. There is no 2018 model year; the 2019 and 2020 cars carry 21V301000 for piston oil rings on the 2.0-litre engine, but have 42 and 23 complaints.

nissan/versa.note: Avoid the 2012 and 2014 Nissan Versa, which have 486 and 337 complaints and scores of 26 and 45, and the 2024 car, an AVOID at 44 on a record still forming; the 2011 car is a CAUTION at 269 complaints. Buy a 2015 to 2021 car: the 2016 has 80 complaints, no recalls and a score of 92. The early cars have two problems. Air Bags is the top category on the 2011 and 2012 cars at 152 and 167 complaints, matched by seven frontal inflator campaigns, most regional, and two side air bag campaigns on the 2012 car. Power Train, the transmission category, is 163 on the 2012 car and leads the 2014 car at 134 with no campaign behind it; the count falls to 47 in 2015 and 20 in 2016. The 2021 car has two campaigns for one electric power steering torque sensor fault, 22V693000 and 23V496000; both must be closed. The 2024 car's 95 complaints are led by Engine at 53.

nissan/murano.note: Avoid the 2015 Nissan Murano, which has 202 complaints, five safety-critical recall campaigns and a score of 37, and treat the 2016 and 2017 cars, at 107 complaints each and scores of 63 and 65, as CAUTION unless every brake campaign is documented. Buy a 2011 to 2013 car, which score 80, 80 and 89, or a 2018 or later car, where the 2018 has 15 complaints and scores 92 and the 2021 to 2024 cars score 91 to 93. The 2015 redesign's problem is the anti-lock braking system: four of its five campaigns cover the ABS actuator, 15V364000 for contamination in the solenoid valve, 16V636000 for cars with Intelligent Cruise Control, 18V601000 for pumps that leak brake fluid onto a circuit board, and 19V807000, which re-covers 2015 to 2018 cars left unrepaired. Power Train leads the 2015 complaints at 52 and Air Bags is second at 36. The 2020 car carries two chassis campaigns, 21V170000 and 21V402000, and the 2025 redesign opens at CAUTION with 21 complaints.

volkswagen/atlas.note: Avoid the 2021 Volkswagen Atlas, which has 461 complaints, twelve recall campaigns and a score of 42, and treat the 2018, 2019 and 2024 cars, at 461, 471 and 167 complaints and scores of 56, 51 and 54, with caution. Buy a 2022 or 2023 car, which have 178 and 130 complaints and score 73 each; the 2020 car scores 87 but on 27 complaints and low evidence. The Atlas has 64 recall campaigns in eight model years. The 2018 list covers a leaking fuel tank, brake caliper pistons and bracket bolts, and an air bag sensor; the 2019 list is dominated by side air bag campaigns, and Air Bags leads that year's complaints at 139. The 2021 car's Electrical System count of 144 matches campaign 21V616000 for damaged fuse box relays that can trigger the horn or starter, and two steering knuckle campaigns, 20V712000 and 21V026000, cover the same year. From 2022 Engine leads at 49 and 35, with 22V753000 for connecting rod bearings.

volkswagen/tiguan.note: Avoid the 2018 and 2022 Volkswagen Tiguan, which have 283 and 252 complaints and scores of 45 and 40, and treat the 2019 car (188 complaints, score 69) with caution. Buy a 2014 to 2017 car, which score 86 to 89 on 62 to 96 complaints, or a 2023 car, which has 60 complaints and scores 84. The first-generation cars are a quiet record whose top category is Air Bags, covered by the frontal air bag debris campaign 15V483000 on 2011 to 2014 cars and the control unit capacitor campaign 19V535000 on 2015 and 2016 cars; all run on premium fuel. The 2018 redesign brought twelve campaigns, mostly assembly faults on the long-wheelbase car, including engine support bolts, a lower ball joint nut and a rear shock absorber weld, and Engine leads the complaints at 81. The 2022 car's Engine count of 105 has no campaign behind it; its one safety-critical recall, 21V853000, is a loose brake pipe nut. The 2025 car opens at CAUTION.

volkswagen/golf.note: Avoid the 2015, 2017 and 2019 Volkswagen Golf, which score 31, 38 and 46 on 131, 187 and 82 complaints, and treat the 2011 and 2016 cars (scores 60 and 50) with caution. Buy a 2012 to 2014 car, which score 77 to 83 on 48, 43 and 11 complaints, or a 2020 or 2021 car, which score 90 and 92 on 6 and 7. The Golf's record is small, 747 complaints across eleven years, so campaigns move the score as much as complaints do, and the 2015 car has twelve, eight safety-critical: four fuel system campaigns including the fuel rail, fuel pump plating and a tank suction pump, plus a camshaft lobe that can shear and disable the brake vacuum pump.
