Fuel/Propulsion System accounts for 55 of the 2017 car's 187 complaints. The 2019 car's are led by Engine at 37 and it carries a safety-critical ignition switch campaign, 23V604000. Campaign 24V110000, issued in 2024, covers every 2015 to 2020 car.

mitsubishi/outlander.note: Avoid the 2015, 2016 and 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, which have 234, 169 and 212 complaints and scores of 38, 34 and 34. Buy a 2011 to 2014 car, which score 79 to 88 on between 36 and 88 complaints, or a 2017 to 2020 car, which score 76 to 85 on between 29 and 55. The 2015 and 2016 cars are a transmission problem: Power Train has 142 and 70 complaints, Engine 47 and 28, and campaign 16V563000 covers the 2016 car's CVT control module while 17V609000 covers 2015 to 2017 cars for starter relays that can cause a stall. Two parking brake corrosion campaigns, 18V070000 and 20V741000, cover the 2014 to 2016 cars. The 2022 redesign is a different pattern: Structure leads at 75 with no campaign to explain it, and the car carries two seat belt retractor campaigns, a fuel pump campaign and three rearview camera campaigns. Most early-car campaigns are corrosion recalls limited to salt-belt states, for frame members, control arms and liftgate gas springs.

mitsubishi/outlander-sport.note: Avoid the 2015 and 2016 Mitsubishi Outlander Sport, which have 232 and 163 complaints and scores of 34 and 36, and treat the 2013 and 2014 cars (scores 67 and 65) with caution. Buy a 2017 or later car: the 2017 has 73 complaints and no recalls, the 2018 has 21, and the 2021 to 2025 cars have between 1 and 17 complaints each with scores of 90 to 93. The bad years are the CVT years. Power Train has 142 complaints on the 2015 car and 65 on the 2016, with Engine at 46 and 27, and campaigns 16V548000 and 16V563000 cover the transmission cooling lines and control module; 17V609000 covers both years for starter relays that can stall the engine. The 2013 car has ten campaigns, four safety-critical, including a seat-mounted air bag on leather-seat cars and a missing fuel sending unit harness on all-wheel-drive cars. After 2016 the only campaign of note is 22V563000, transmission software on 2019 to 2022 cars.

subaru/ascent.note: Avoid the 2019 and 2020 Subaru Ascent, which have 439 and 319 complaints and scores of 32 and 36. Buy a 2021 or later car: the 2021 has 100 complaints and scores 81, and the 2022 has 55 and scores 87, the best on the nameplate. The first two years are an electrical and transmission record. Electrical System leads with 161 and 101 complaints, and campaign 22V907000 covers 2019 to 2022 cars for a cabin heater ground bolt that can melt its terminal. Power Train is second at 87 and 57, matched by 19V855000 for a transmission hydraulic sensor on the 2019 car and 21V955000 for a transmission control unit programming error on 2019 and 2020 cars. The 2019 car alone has nine campaigns, including missing B-pillar spot welds, a crankcase ventilation valve that can enter the engine, and loose driveshaft bolts, and both years carry the fuel pump campaign 21V587000. Visibility/Wiper is 66 and 49 complaints with no campaign behind it. From 2021 no category dominates.

subaru/legacy.note: Avoid the 2020 Subaru Legacy, which has 121 complaints, six recall campaigns and a score of 45, and treat the 2015 to 2019 cars, all CAUTION with between 117 and 159 complaints, the same way. Buy a 2021 or later car, where the 2021 has 31 complaints and scores 86 and the 2023 has 10 and scores 90, or a 2013 or 2014 car with its air bag inflator recall list confirmed. The 2015 to 2020 cars are a plateau: Electrical System leads the 2015, 2016 and 2018 cars at 37, 51 and 40, and Visibility/Wiper leads the 2017, 2019 and 2020 cars at 33, 49 and 57 with no campaign behind it. The 2020 redesign added two transmission control unit campaigns, 21V955000 and 22V485000, a brake pedal bracket bolt and an occupant detection sensor capacitor, 24V227000, that can disable the passenger air bag on 2020 to 2022 cars. The 2013 and 2014 cars have 66 and 53 complaints but twelve and ten campaigns, seven of them Takata inflator recalls.

hyundai/kona.note: The Hyundai Kona has no year to avoid: every one of its eight model years is a BUY, from a score of 93 on the 2018 car to 74 on the 2024. The strongest years are the 2018, with 74 complaints and no recalls, and the 2021 to 2023 cars at 85, 85 and 86; the weakest are the 2019 and 2020, at 187 and 156 complaints and 81 each. Engine is the top category from 2018 to 2022, at 41, 128, 103, 76 and 32, and the one campaign that matches it is 21V301000, covering 2019 to 2021 cars with the 2.0-litre engine for piston oil rings that were not properly heat-treated. From 2023 Electrical System takes over at 25 and 31, and the 2024 redesign carries four campaigns, three safety-critical: chafing 12-volt battery cables, rear seat belt assemblies and a rear centre seat belt buckle, plus an exhaust gas recirculation valve that can cut drive power. Those campaigns, not the 50 complaints, hold the 2024 score down.

hyundai/genesis.note: Avoid the 2015 Hyundai Genesis, which has 305 complaints, six recall campaigns and a score of 39, and treat the 2012 car (269 complaints, score 59) with caution. Buy a 2014 car, which has 23 complaints and no recalls and scores 97 on low evidence, or a 2016 car, which has 102 complaints and scores 75; the 2011 and 2013 cars score 73 and 71. The 2012 and 2013 cars are led by Engine at 71 and 66 with Service Brakes at 65 and 58, and campaign 13V489000 covers the 2011 and 2012 cars for brake fluid that lets the hydraulic control unit corrode. The 2015 second-generation sedan is an electrical record: Electrical System has 113 complaints, and its campaigns cover water leaking into the rear lamps and corrupting the gear display, an instrument cluster that can show the wrong speed, an ABS module that can short circuit, and a starter solenoid that admits water and can start an engine fire. Several campaigns here also cover the Genesis Coupe.

hyundai/santa-fe-sport.note: Avoid the 2017 and 2018 Hyundai Santa Fe Sport, which have 345 and 415 complaints and scores of 41 and 37. Buy a 2015 or 2016 car, which have 82 and 66 complaints and score 87 and 93; the 2013 and 2014 cars score 72 and 78 once their campaigns are closed. Engine is the top category in all six years, at 108, 93, 41, 41, 197 and 240. On the 2013 and 2014 cars that count has a campaign behind it, 17V226000, for machining errors that cause premature bearing wear, with 18V934000 covering a fuel pipe damaged during that repair. On the 2017 and 2018 cars there is no engine campaign at all: no free repair, and no way to identify an affected car by VIN. The other pattern is the ABS module: 20V520000 and 21V303000 cover 2013 to 2015 cars for brake fluid leaking inside it, and 22V056000 and 22V810000 cover the 2017 and 2018 cars for a short circuit that can cause an engine compartment fire.

kia/telluride.note: The Kia Telluride has no AVOID year, but the 2020 car, with 748 complaints, 124.7 per year on the road and a CAUTION at 66, is the one to think twice about. Buy a 2021 or 2023 car, which have 354 and 203 complaints and score 82 and 79; the 2024 and 2025 cars score 76 and 79 but at 107.0 and 105.0 complaints per year on the road. The 2020 car's complaints spread across Exterior Lighting at 183, matched by campaign 24V148000 for failing high beams, and Engine and Visibility/Wiper at 138 and 135 with no campaign behind them. Three campaigns cover every 2020 to 2024 car: 24V407000 for a power seat motor that can overheat and cause a fire, 26V430000 for the same fault after improper repairs, and 24V214000 for a driveshaft that may not be fully engaged and can let the car roll away in Park. The 2024 car adds 24V077000 for valve springs that can break and hole the block.

chevrolet/volt.note: Avoid the 2017 Volt, which has 695 complaints and a score of 47 against 93 complaints and a score of 94 for the 2014; the years to buy are 2014, 2015 and 2019, and 2013 and 2018 are CAUTION verdicts. The first-generation car (2011 to 2015) settles after a 2013 with 308 complaints, and the second generation from 2016 has one bad year in an otherwise clean run. The 2013 car's 161 Air Bags complaints line up with 23V516000, a driver air bag inflator recall, and it also carries 18V397000 for a control module update that disabled battery cell balancing and 15V145000 for a battery that can drain if the driver leaves the car switched on. The 2017 car's complaints are Electrical System at 309, Fuel/Propulsion System at 233, Power Train at 219 and Engine at 181, a propulsion-system pattern with no recall campaign behind it. The 2018 car falls to 222 complaints and the 2019 to 34, with only seat belt and brake caliper campaigns on those years.

chevrolet/bolt-ev.note: No Bolt EV year is an AVOID, but the 2019 and 2020 cars are CAUTION verdicts at 66 and 56, and the years to buy are 2021 and 2023, which both score 80, once the battery recall paperwork is complete. The 2017 and 2018 cars have no complaints on file and are DATA PENDING. Electrical System is the top component in every scored year, 85 on the 2019 car and 93 on the 2020, and the recalls explain it: 20V701000 and 21V560000 cover the 2019 car for a high-voltage battery that could catch fire when charged to full, 21V650000 extends that to the 2020 to 2022 cars, and 24V481000 and 24V812000 recall those cars again because the diagnostic software fitted under the earlier campaign may have failed. Every Bolt from 2019 to 2023 also carries 22V930000 and 23V845000 for a seat belt pretensioner exhaust that can ignite carpet fibres after a crash. The 2020 car has eight recalls, five safety-critical; the 2022 has seven; the 2023 has three.

nissan/leaf.note: Avoid the 2015 Leaf, a CAUTION at 65 with 109 complaints, 85 of them Service Brakes; buy a 2012, 2014 or 2018, which score 94, 84 and 78. Every other scored year is a BUY, and the whole record holds only 442 complaints. Service Brakes is the top component on the 2012 to 2015 cars, and 16V119000 covers the 2013 to 2015 Leaf for a relay inside the electronic brake booster that may freeze in very cold weather; the 2013 to 2015 cars also carry the occupant detection and air bag campaigns 13V069000, 14V138000 and 16V244000. The second-generation 2018 car has 66 complaints with Service Brakes at 19 and Electrical System at 18, and 23V494000 covers the 2018 to 2023 cars for unintended acceleration if the driving mode is changed after cruise control is disengaged. The 2017 and 2023 cars score 89 and 88 with no complaints on file and low evidence; the 2024 and 2025 cars are DATA PENDING.

mini/cooper.note: No Mini Cooper year is an AVOID: every scored year is a BUY, from 80 for the 2013 car to 95 for the 2014, and the 2014, with 66 complaints and no recalls, is the one to buy. The record covers only 2011 to 2015 and 2025; the 2016 to 2024 cars have no complaints on file and are DATA PENDING, an absent record rather than a clean one. Electrical System is the top component on the 2011 to 2013 cars at 41, 56 and 57 complaints, with Air Bags second or third at 19, 25 and 35, and the one campaign on those years is 23V337000, a safety-critical Electrical System recall limited to cars sold or registered in a list of states. The 2014 car's complaints spread evenly, Electrical System, Engine and Power Train at 16 each. The 2015 car climbs to 106 complaints, Engine at 28, with no recall behind them. The 2025 car scores 90 on low evidence with one seat belt campaign, 25V616000.

mazda/cx-9.note: Avoid the 2011 and 2012 CX-9, CAUTION verdicts at 65 and 50 with Service Brakes accounting for 100 of the 2011 car's 170 complaints and 143 of the 2012 car's 221; buy a 2014, 2015, 2017 or any year from 2019 to 2022, which score between 83 and 93. The 2018 car is a CAUTION at 57 with 126 complaints, 74 of them Engine. The brake pattern on the first-generation cars has no recall behind it; their campaigns are the passenger air bag inflator (18V717000, 17V429000, 17V457000 and 19V782000) and 15V451000 for front ball joints that corrode when water enters the fitting. Engine becomes the top component from 2014 on, 61 on the 2016 car and 43 on the 2017, neither with a recall, then 74 on the 2018, where 19V403000 covers a wiring harness that can disable the engine starting system and 21V875000 a fuel pump impeller that may crack. The 2020 and 2022 cars have 19 and 9 complaints and score 93 on low evidence.

chrysler/town-and-country.note: No Town and Country year is an AVOID: all six years from 2011 to 2016 are BUY verdicts, and the 2015, at 86 on 382 complaints with no safety-critical recall, is the one to buy. The other years score 72 to 79 on heavy counts, 773 complaints on the 2011 car and never fewer than 522 in any year but 2015. Electrical System dominates the 2011 to 2014 cars at 523, 395, 393 and 215, and the matching campaign is 14V234000, for a vent window switch that may overheat on the 2011 to 2014 cars; the 2013 car also carries 13V283000 and 13V291000 for air bag software. Power Train takes over on the 2015 and 2016 cars at 113 and 186, and 16V461000 recalled the 2015 and 2016 automatic transmissions. The Dodge Grand Caravan shares the platform and the campaigns, and its 2016 car is an AVOID at 38 on 1,156 complaints where the Town and Country's 2016 scores 77 on 522.

kia/sportage.note: Avoid the 2017 and 2023 Sportage, AVOID verdicts at 46 and 33 on 399 and 187 complaints; buy a 2014 to 2016 or a 2018 to 2022, which score between 73 and 91. The 2012 and 2013 cars are CAUTION at 65 and 66, and the 2024 and 2025 cars are CAUTION at 67 and 60 on thinner evidence. Engine is the top component in every year from 2011 to 2022, at 328 and 300 of the 2012 and 2013 cars' 392 and 380 complaints, and 17V224000 covers the 2011 to 2013 engines for machining errors that cause premature bearing wear, with 18V907000 covering 2011 to 2018 cars that received a replacement engine. The 2017 car has Engine at 219 and carries 21V137000, for a brake control unit that can short and cause an engine compartment fire. The redesigned 2023 car has six recalls, four safety-critical, among them 23V410000 for a brake booster diaphragm and 22V651000 for an alternator nut that can stall the engine.

volkswagen/passat.note: Avoid the 2012 to 2015 Passat, four AVOID verdicts at 26, 26, 26 and 47; buy a 2016 or 2017, which score 81 and 72 on medium evidence, and treat the 2018 to 2022 cars' scores of 87 to 95 as promising rather than proven, because every one is on low evidence. Air Bags is the top component on the 2012 to 2015 cars at 295, 382, 354 and 88, and the driver frontal air bag inflator campaigns 16V078000, 18V148000 and 19V862000 on the 2012 to 2014 cars, with 19V014000 on the 2015, account for it; 15V483000 covers the same years for debris in the frontal air bag. The 2012 and 2013 cars are rated on diesel and carry 16V171000 for a corroding underbody sensor connector and 17V309000 for a heat shield on diesel cars with the direct-shift transmission. The 2016 car has 106 complaints and the 2017 has 109. From 2018 the counts are 45, 12, 15, 0 and 12.

honda/accord-hybrid.note: Avoid the 2014, 2015, 2019 and 2023 Accord Hybrid, AVOID verdicts at 46, 46, 32 and 47; buy a 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021 or 2022, which score 89, 80, 79, 84 and 88. The 2024 car is a CAUTION at 61 and the 2025 scores 81 on low evidence. The 2014 car has 954 complaints, 79.5 per year on road, with Electrical System at 376 and Engine at 176, and 15V602000 covers the 2014 and 2015 cars for electrical interference that can put the hybrid system into fail-safe mode and disable the petrol engine. The 2019 car has 529 complaints spread across Forward Collision Avoidance at 96, Engine at 93, Electrical System at 85 and Service Brakes at 81. The 2023 car has 139 complaints and six recalls, including 23V588000 for a transmission that can lose drive and 25V785000 for a control module that may reset while driving. The petrol Accord is an AVOID in 2018 at 30, the year the hybrid scores 80.

hyundai/sonata-hybrid.note: No Sonata Hybrid year is an AVOID: eleven of the thirteen scored years are BUY verdicts, the 2018 and 2019 cars score 94, and the 2012 and 2016 cars are CAUTION at 59 and 62. The whole record holds 741 complaints against 11,270 for the petrol Sonata, and the hybrid beats the petrol car's score in every shared year from 2011 to 2017. Engine is the top component in the busier years, 67 on the 2012 car and 72 on the 2016, and the campaigns match: 20V746000 covers the 2011 to 2013 and 2016 cars for connecting rod bearings that wear prematurely, and 21V727000 covers the 2017. The 2011 to 2015 cars also carry 17V152000 and 17V617000 for front seat belt linkages that may detach from the pretensioners, and 23V651000 for the anti-lock brake control unit. From 2018 the counts are 9, 4, 0, 53 and 19 complaints, and only the 2021 car is on medium evidence; the 2023 and 2024 cars are DATA PENDING, and the 2025 scores 83.

ford/escape-hev.note: Avoid the 2020 and 2021 Escape hybrid, AVOID verdicts at 47 on 287 and 335 complaints; buy a 2022, which scores 79 on 66 complaints, or a 2023 to 2025, which score 91, 92 and 92 on low evidence. Structure is the top component in both bad years, 105 on the 2020 car and 91 on the 2021, and no campaign in that category explains it. The hybrid's own page lists no recall campaigns, but the hybrid-specific campaigns are recorded on the petrol Escape's page and apply to these cars: 22V484000 for engine failures on 2020 to 2022 hybrids that can release oil and fuel vapour, 24V330000 for hybrid powertrain software that can shift into neutral and lose drive, and 22V331000 for welds inside the 2020 car's high-voltage battery. The petrol 2020 Escape scores 26 on 1,517 complaints, so the hybrid is the better 2020 car without being a good one.

toyota/rav4-hybrid.note: Avoid the 2017 RAV4 Hybrid, an AVOID at 48 on 302 complaints with Electrical System at 107; buy any other year, since the 2016 and 2018 to 2025 cars all score between 76 and 93. The whole record holds 408 complaints, and every year except 2017 is on low evidence, so the scores rest on small numbers. The 2019 and 2020 cars share the petrol RAV4's campaigns, 20V064000 for porosity in the engine castings, 20V286000 for front lower suspension arms that may crack and 20V373000 for water entering the steering gear box, yet have only 22 and 13 complaints against the petrol car's 873 and 628. The 2021 car's 22 complaints are led by Air Bags at 17. The 2017 car's 302 complaints and Electrical System at 107 mirror the petrol 2017 car's 305 and 107 almost exactly, so nothing in the record separates the two except the score. The 2024 car has one complaint and scores 91.
